recentItems.title: Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev Says It Took Rivals 10 to 15 Years to Catch up to Him (Part 2)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 1: https://youtu.be/8YYmtZYQ0Aw
--------
Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev sits down with DJ Vlad to explain how the fintech app reshaped stock investing after he and Baiju Bhatt moved on from Kronos and launched Robinhood in California in 2013. Tenev breaks down the logic behind commission-free trading, why E-Trade and legacy brokerages were slow to change, and how electronic markets made trades cost a fraction of a penny to process. He also discusses Silicon Valley influences like Instagram, Uber, Facebook, and Snapchat, plus Robinhood’s early bet on Amazon Web Services when major financial firms still relied on physical data centers. From New York trading infrastructure to San Francisco startup culture, Tenev details how cloud technology, automated identity checks, and instant onboarding let users buy stocks in minutes—an experience he says competitors took 10 to 15 years to match. A concise look at investing, fintech disruption, and Robinhood’s rise.

recentItems.title: Vincent “Gigi” Marino: Judge Added 25 Years Even After the Jury Found Him Not Guilty (Part 3)
recentItems.description:

Part 2: https://youtu.be/3KdbDAzBMx4
Part 1: https://youtu.be/gKnZIQpWXOc
--------
Vincent “Gigi” Marino sits down with Vlad to discuss the 1989 IHOP shooting of New England mob boss Frank Salemme, the RICO trials that followed, and the sentencing decision he says added 25 years after a jury found the attempted murder allegation not proven beyond a reasonable doubt. Marino breaks down the Patriarca crime family war, Salemme’s rise after Raymond Patriarca Jr. and Junior Russo, and the fallout involving John Connolly, Whitey Bulger, Stephen Flemmi, Bobby DeLuca, and FBI informant allegations tied to Boston organized crime. He also addresses the Souza murder enhancement, claims about withheld discovery, Judge Wolf’s courtroom, perjury issues, witness protection, and the legal arguments around double jeopardy and statute of limitations. In a rare admission, Marino discusses his role in the Salemme shooting and why he says the violence unfolded during one of the most chaotic eras in the New England Mafia.

recentItems.title: Dale Comstock on Never Killing Hand-to-Hand Despite 200 Street Fights & MMA Career (Part 11)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 10: https://youtu.be/TJYeOXUWAks
Part 1: https://youtu.be/U21AbA_cZII
--------
Dale Comstock sits down with Vlad to address a direct question: after military combat involving rifles, mortars, and long-distance engagements, has he ever killed someone in hand-to-hand combat? Comstock says no, explaining that true hand-to-hand lethal encounters are rare, even among seasoned operators. He shares a cautionary story about a friend working abroad with a group of SEALs who became separated and ended up grappling with a Taliban fighter after his rifle sling failed. The encounter ended only after the operator managed to access a knife he had never properly trained with.

Comstock connects the story to hard-earned lessons on weapons, preparation, ego, and survival. Despite more than 200 street fights, a professional MMA background, and a sixth-degree black belt, he emphasizes the difference between fighting, controlling someone, and killing hand-to-hand.

--------
Marine veteran and scout sniper Cody Alford sits down with Vlad to reflect on combat in Fallujah, the Iraq War, and the moral weight carried by service members after battle. Alford discusses rules of engagement, civilian casualties, PTSD, military mental health, and why he believes war offers no “clean” outcome. The conversation also addresses insurgents exploiting civilians, including reports of children being used to trigger IEDs or placed in danger as human shields. Vlad references past interviews with Robert O’Neill and Dale Comstock, including debates over the Osama bin Laden raid and acceptable risk in high-value target missions. Alford also breaks down Operation Steel Curtain, describing Marine Expeditionary Unit movements from San Diego through Hawaii and the shift toward booby traps, vehicle-borne IEDs, tunnels, and urban guerrilla tactics across Iraq.

--------
Former Army Ranger sniper Nicholas Irving joins Shawn Prez for a sharp discussion on Iran, Tehran’s strategy, and whether U.S. officials are overstating claims about the country’s economic collapse. Irving argues that reports suggesting Iran is too broke to outlast America may be another layer of wartime propaganda, questioning how much the public can trust narratives about sanctions, frozen assets, nuclear threats, and military readiness.

The conversation touches on tough talk from Iran, Donald Trump-era rhetoric, Barack Obama’s past negotiations, alleged funding to groups like the Houthis, and comparisons to North Korea-style hardship. Irving challenges assumptions about Iran’s economy, asking who has actually been on the ground in Tehran to verify what Americans are being told.

Watch as Irving breaks down diplomacy, war messaging, Middle East power dynamics, and why claims about Iran “running out of money” deserve deeper scrutiny.
